messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Finova performance SLOs & regional routing

Hi Olivia / Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we all have the same picture: 

Call highlights / what I heard:
- Primary goal: deploy LLM-based customer support assistant with strict latency and data residency needs across US, EU, and APAC.
- Target SLOs discussed: p95 latency goal for short responses (~<=64 tokens) in the 200-400ms range depending on region; streaming for longer outputs with low first-byte latency.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~150 RPS, peak up to ~600 RPS during batch hours; concurrency requirement: ~200-300 concurrent user sessions.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU; APAC customers should be routed to a Singapore/Japan region.

Immediate questions / clarifications we promised to follow up on:
1) Concrete region-level SLO targets (p95) you want us to design for (US/EU/APAC).
2) Typical prompt/response size and whether streaming is required for the majority of responses.
3) Desired concurrency / sustained throughput and expected daily traffic pattern (peaks by hour).
4) Any procurement or security gating items (SOC 2, KMS BYOK, VPC peering) we should include in the mutual action plan.

What Redwood can offer (short list):
- Hosted API + regional routing for low-latency endpoints (we can pin models in region).
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in region (eu-west / ap-southeast / us-west) with autoscaling and guaranteed capacity.
- Private/VPC options and BYOK for EU residency and strict egress controls.
- Streaming (chunked responses) over HTTP/gRPC for real-time UX; prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated compute for common prompts.

Proposed next steps:
- Olivia / Samir: confirm the concrete p95 targets per region and whether streaming is required for all long-form flows.
- Redwood (Marcus + Aditya): propose a first-cut capacity plan and recommended cluster sizing (per-region) based on your numbers; follow-up technical deep dive with your infra/security folks.
- Put together a 2-week PoC plan (traffic capture + small dedicated capacity) to validate latencies under real traffic.

Attachments: I attached the network diagram we asked for and our initial SLA draft for your legal team to review.

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus in on the technical answers.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side so you can size accurately: 

Region-specific SLOs (final asks):
- US (NA customers): p95 <= 300ms for responses <= 64 tokens.
- EU (EU customers): p95 <= 350ms for responses <= 64 tokens; data residency requirement: all customer input and derived artifacts must remain in EU (no egress to US).
- APAC (SG/JP): p95 <= 400ms desired for short responses; hard requirement is first-byte < 250ms for streaming flows in APAC.

Throughput & concurrency (baseline vs peak):
- Baseline sustained: 150 RPS globally.
- Peak: up to 600 RPS during business hours (spikes can be short, ~5-10 mins).
- Concurrent sessions: expect ~300 simultaneous interactive sessions during peak.

Streaming & payloads:
- Typical prompts: 80-120 tokens in; average completion length ~120-300 tokens.
- Streaming is required for our chat UX — users expect near-real-time typing. First-byte (time-to-first-chunk) is critical.

Security / compliance asks:
- EU data must not leave EU; backups and audit logs must be stored in-region.
- We require customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for production keys and an audited key-rotation policy.
- Please include SOC 2 Type II evidence and answers to a short vendor questionnaire (I’ll share the questionnaire).

Next steps from our side: I’ll share the security questionnaire and connect our infra lead (CCing Samir) into the technical deep dive. Also looping in procurement — they’ll want the preliminary SLA and estimated TCO.

Olivia

Hi Olivia / Samir — Marcus from Redwood SE team. Thanks for the clarifications — below are technical answers and a recommended starting configuration to validate your SLOs.

Quick answers to the asks:
- Regional deployment: we can provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west (Frankfurt), us-west (Oregon), and ap-southeast (Singapore). For strict EU residency, we will keep model inputs, outputs, caches, and logs in the EU cluster; backups/archives can be restricted to EU storage only.
- Latency: the p95 numbers you listed are achievable with regional pinned capacity + streaming enabled. For short responses (<=64 tokens) we typically see p95 in the 150-300ms range on optimized RTX-class GPUs when the model variant is quantized and KV cache is warm.
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming over both HTTP chunked responses and gRPC streaming. We aim for time-to-first-chunk <150ms with a warmed model and proper batching settings.

Recommended starter sizing (rough):
- Baseline traffic (150 RPS): 2 x dedicated GPU nodes per region (Nvidia A10/A16 class equivalent) with autoscaling to handle bursts.
- Peak handling (600 RPS spikes): autoscale to ~6-8 nodes across regions; for APAC peak we recommend 3 dedicated nodes to keep first-byte under 250ms.
- Concurrency: configure request concurrency limits per node; we recommend starting with concurrency_per_node=8 and per-request token caps to limit tail latency.
- Batching: continuous batching with max batch size ~32 for interactive flows. With this config, expected throughput per GPU (for your prompt sizes) is ~1000-2000 tokens/sec depending on model and quantization.

Data residency & encryption:
- BYOK: We support customer-managed KMS keys per-region; keys never leave region and are used for at-rest encryption of logs/artefacts.
- Audit trails: we can stream audit logs to your EU logging bucket and provide log retention policies per your compliance needs.
- Network: VPC peering and private endpoints available for Dedicated; we can lock egress to only your approved endpoints.

Fallback & routing strategy:
- Smart routing: we recommend routing by user region to the nearest regional cluster. For resilience, requests can fallback to a cross-region read-only replica (with explicit consent for data flow) or a smaller hosted model variant (only for non-sensitive flows).
- Warm caches & pre-warming: for predictable peaks, we can pre-warm KV caches and keep one or two hot replicas to reduce cold-start tail latency.

Suggested POC approach:
1) 1-week dedicated trial in EU and APAC with 2 nodes each; replay 24 hours of captured traffic at 2x to measure p95 and streaming first-byte.
2) Collect token-level latency and per-route traces; iterate batching and concurrency settings.
3) Finalize SLA language and procurement items (BYOK, SOC2 artifacts).

Deliverables I can prepare for the deep dive:
- Region-specific capacity plan (node counts + expected p95 estimates)
- Network diagram + VPC peering instructions (I referenced the draft network diagram you shared).
- SOC2 evidence pack and security questionnaire responses.

If this looks good, can we schedule a technical deep dive (Marcus + infra lead + our infra engineer) next Tue 10am CET / 1am PT? I can also bring our infra engineer to discuss VPC/KMS specifics.

Regards,
